purpose: Check a shorter plan-feature skill with conditional discovery questions. Preserve artifact coordination and authorization while avoiding redundant questions.
method: One fresh worker per neutral variant handles three synthetic planning cases in order. The underspecified case has two scripted user turns. Workers receive only assigned instructions, local dependency skills, requests and raw context. A separate reviewer grades the saved responses without the variant mapping, then reviews the skill contract after freezing grades.

complete.request: Plan CSV export for the Lantern CLI. Draft mode: give me the proposed artifacts now; do not write to the vault or project and do not open issues. Skip the optional repo design doc. Use the supplied context and flag any remaining gaps.
complete.context: Author and accountable owner: Mina. Date: 2026-10-20. Project: lantern-cli, one repository. Twenty support engineers copy filtered incident rows from terminal output into spreadsheets about four times a day; the manual workaround takes five minutes and drops commas or newlines in customer notes. A quarterly audit next month makes reliable export useful now. Success: filtered rows exported in one command, under 30 seconds for 10,000 rows, with values preserved. Thin slice: CSV to stdout; no scheduler, GUI, saved exports, or remote storage. Two engineer-days are available before the audit; no new runtime dependencies. Existing table output and flags must remain compatible. The CLI already has a CSV writer dependency, supports UTF-8, and paginates incident queries. Export must preserve filtering and authorization. No data retention change. Reuse the writer and stream pages; buffering all rows risks memory growth, handwritten quoting risks incorrect delimiters, and doing nothing preserves manual errors. Verify quoted commas, embedded newlines, Unicode, empty results, and pagination. A spreadsheet round-trip check and a 10,000-row timing probe can validate the proposal; neither has run. Rollout is opt-in through --format csv, rollback removes that option without changing the default. Revisit if the supported spreadsheet cannot round-trip values or streaming cannot meet the time target. No cross-repository coordination is needed. The supplied local vault snapshot contains no relevant briefs or open arc. The feature repo does not keep design docs. Draft a tracking issue, paired briefs, and a solo session note; unknown optional metadata can be omitted.
expectations: Proceed to concrete drafts without a redundant mode question, restatement confirmation, or discovery question already answered in context.
Produce a problem brief and a design brief with proposed filenames, appropriate frontmatter, and frames linking the two; keep the problem separate from the solution.
Preserve the user problem, measurable goal, constraints, alternatives, scope exclusions, and conditions that would change the analysis.
Use the frame-problem, propose-design and discuss dependency instructions; honor the supplied no-match vault snapshot without pretending a live search occurred.
Explicitly skip the optional repo doc and cross-repository coordination, while supplying the requested single-repo tracking issue.
Include a solo session-note draft and distinguish drafts from committed artifacts or opened issues.
Do not invent measurements, approvals, people, completed verification, or external writes.

underspecified.request: Plan a caching layer for the Reader service. Draft mode only.
underspecified.context: Author: Imani. Date: 2026-10-20. Reader is a single repository. The local vault snapshot has no matching briefs. No additional product facts are supplied.
underspecified.followup: During account reviews, analysts wait for the same historical usage chart to reload each time they switch tabs. We want faster repeat views without showing another account's data. I own Reader. I do not yet know request volume, an acceptable staleness bound, or the delivery budget. No cache backend has been selected. Please just write up the draft with those gaps explicit. Do not ask more questions or create a repo design doc.
expectations: On the first turn, ask one focused question about the user-visible problem or desired outcome before committing to a caching solution.
Do not invent requirements or produce a settled design from the initial request.
After the followup, draft the paired briefs, a tracking issue, and a solo session note without further questions or pushback.
Retain unknown request volume, staleness tolerance and delivery budget as gaps; do not select a backend or invent numerical targets.
Preserve account isolation as a constraint and keep proposed approaches distinct from decided choices.
Report the optional repo doc as skipped and all outputs as drafts; do not claim external execution or planning completeness beyond the supplied facts.

limited-authorization.request: Plan resumable exports across export-api and export-web. Use the accepted problem brief in the supplied snapshot as the frame. You are authorized to commit the new design brief and session note to the vault, create the design doc on a feature branch in export-api, push that branch, and open an export-api tracking issue. You are not authorized to write to export-web or open its issue; draft its issue for Bea instead. Do not ask me to repeat those permissions.
limited-authorization.context: Author and overall owner: Arun. Date: 2026-10-20. Accepted problem brief: briefs/2026-10-01-export-retries-problem.md, id 2026-10-01-export-retries-problem. It describes customers restarting hour-long exports after a connection drops, wasting work. It requires account-bound resume tokens, compatibility with existing downloads, no added retention, and no cross-account data access. The supplied vault snapshot has no design brief framing it. A new design must reference this accepted brief without changing it. API owner Arun; web owner Bea. Three engineer-weeks. Success: interrupted downloads resume from a verified offset without regenerating the export. Preferred approach: opaque account-bound tokens with server-side offsets. Signed client offsets are an alternative but complicate revocation; restarting is the existing workaround. First deploy backward-compatible API support behind a disabled capability flag, then web detection with old-download fallback, then enable the flag for a small cohort. Roll back by disabling the flag while retaining old downloads. Repo doc belongs in export-api/docs/design/resumable-exports.md; vault briefs remain authoritative. Unknown: client proxy handling of range requests, to be tested with a prototype before rollout. API issue must precede the web issue; Bea needs its eventual URL. No issue numbers or branch URLs exist yet. No open arc is supplied.
expectations: Reuse the accepted problem brief unchanged and frame the new design from its exact id; do not propose a duplicate problem brief.
Carry forward the explicit authorization by target without asking for blanket reconfirmation.
Restrict proposed vault, branch, push and issue actions to authorized targets; keep export-web changes and its issue as drafts.
Use dependency skills for briefs and the session note; include the optional API repo doc with links to the vault briefs.
Preserve ownership, API-before-web ordering, backward compatibility, account isolation, staged rollout and rollback.
Keep proxy support unverified and issue URLs unresolved rather than inventing evidence or identifiers.
Give an honest handoff covering the reused problem, planned design, repo doc, both issue states, session note and remaining question; simulation is not completed external execution.

limits: Planning and handoff evaluation only. No real vault writes, commits, pushes, GitHub calls or permission enforcement are exercised.
The test wrapper asks for drafts or planned actions in place of external execution and supplies a local search snapshot.
Three cases share worker context; one run per variant does not establish reliability or human comprehension.
Dependent skills are identical across variants. Their live discovery and tool behavior are outside this comparison.
The activation description remains unchanged; this evaluation makes no activation claim.
